Article Title: Apple Pay launches in India; here's how to set it up and where you can use it
Article Text:
Apple Pay launched in India: How it works, and who can use it

How to set up and use Apple Pay

Where you can use it

Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users, with Mac support coming soon. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs marking a significant milestone in India’s fast-growing digital payments ecosystem. At launch, Apple Pay supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, enabling payments at thousands of merchants across India and anywhere NFC transactions are accepted globally.Apple also emphasised that privacy remains central to how Apple Pay functions. When a card is added, the actual card number is never stored on the device or Apple's servers, nor shared with merchants during a transaction. Instead, the system assigns a unique Device Account Number, which is encrypted and stored securely within the device's Secure Element — a certified, industry-standard chip built specifically to protect payment information.Presently, Apple Pay is exclusively available to customers holding Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, letting them add those cards to Apple Pay and use them at thousands of in-store and online merchants across India, as well as anywhere that accepts NFC transactions.Jennifer Bailey, Apple's vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, framed the launch as a natural fit for India's fast-growing digital economy, pointing to the country's dynamic, digitally savvy population that's increasingly embracing cashless payments while expecting strong security and privacy standards. She described Apple Pay's core value proposition as making everyday card payments easy, secure, and private — from a simple tap in stores without needing a separate app, PIN, or OTP, to checking out online without repeatedly re-entering payment details.Apple Pay is easy to set up. Customers can add a card directly to Apple Wallet via the latest version of the Axis Bank app. Alternatively, simply open the Wallet app on iPhone, tap the plus sign, and follow the steps to add an eligible card. Once a user adds a card to their Apple device, they can start using Apple Pay right away.Using Apple Pay in stores is seamless and easy. Simply double-click the side button or Home button; authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode if prompted; and hold the top of the iPhone or display of the Apple Watch near the contactless reader to pay. When using Apple Pay, users will continue to earn the rewards and benefits offered by their cards.At launch, Apple Pay will be accepted at millions of merchants across India, including Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato, among others. Apple has also partnered with several payment service providers, including Cashfree, JusPay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline, to extend Apple Pay's reach across their respective merchant networks, with more merchants and apps expected to be added over time.Globally, Apple Pay is now available in more than 90 countries and regions, working with over 11,000 bank and network partners worldwide — making India one of the more prominent recent additions to that global rollout.
Article Summary: Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. The company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs.

Article Title: Pebble launches Qore Ultra wellness band at introductory price of Rs 5,999
Article Text:
Pebble Qore Ultra

Pebble Qore Ultra features

Pebble Qore Ultra price and availability

Home-grown consumer electronics brand Pebble has launched Qore Ultra, its flagship wellness band. In a press release, the company said that the device is designed for continuous, distraction-free wear. Coming with 3 ATM water-resistant design, Qore Ultra integrates a 4-PD precision sensor array and 6-axis motion sensors. “This hardware architecture enables 24x7 tracking of vital metrics, including heart rate, HRV, SpO2, respiration, and stress, while delivering up to 15 days of continuous battery life,” it stated.The band features automatic workout detection for activities like walking and running, over 100 sports modes, and in-app GPS sports tracking. The Pebble Qore mobile application acts as the central hub for this health intelligence, seamlessly translating complex data into intuitive metrics. Users can gauge their daily preparedness through a 0-100 Readiness Score, factoring in HRV, sleep quality, and stress, while monitoring their real-time stamina via the Body Energy Score. For long-term health tracking, the platform calculates Body Age every three days and uses GPS-tracked runs to estimate VO2 Max and Fitness Age.Komal Agarwal, Co-founder of Pebble said “The Pebble Qore series has become one of India's top fitness bands, and the Qore Ultra represents the flagship evolution of that journey. We have put a significant amount of R&D into giving users actionable data that can help them improve their daily rest, activity, and habits. By providing these comprehensive insights alongside community features on our new app, we are shifting the focus from isolated tracking to shared wellness management. ”Pebble Qore Ultra will be available from October 2, 2026 in three color options, Desert Gold, Deep Black, and Deep Blue. Priced at an introductory Rs 5,999 (MRP 8,999), the wearable will be available through Pebble's official website, Flipkart, Amazon, and leading retail stores across the country.

Article Title: A North Dakota farm kid turned ag-tech entrepreneur; his company puts real farm maps on children's play rugs
Article Text:
Representative Image of a colorful map-themed play rug featuring various agricultural fields and farm buildings (AI Generated Image)

From a North Dakota farm to agricultural mapping

How the play-rug idea began

What Boundri sells today

The " carpet farming " idea

A North Dakota farm kid has turned real agricultural maps into children's play rugs, giving toy tractors and combines a miniature version of the landscapes they come from. Nathan Faleide, founder of Boundri, grew up on a farm in North Dakota and around agricultural mapping through his family's Satshot business. Boundri was started in 2022 and grew from a play rug Faleide made for his children into a company that now puts personalised maps on rugs and other products. Today, Boundri sells mapped play rugs, blankets, wall maps, prints and other customised products, while its mapping background stretches back decades through the Faleide family's work in agricultural technology.Faleide's connection to farming began early. On Boundri's current About Us page, he says he grew up on a farm in North Dakota and that farm toys were central to his daily routine. He also says he "did farm a little" himself, but adds that it "wasn't my time." At the same time, he grew up around agricultural mapping through his family's company, Satshot. Faleide says that experience helped develop his expertise in software and maps, eventually providing the technical background behind Boundri.Satshot's history dates to 1994, when Lanny Faleide, Nathan's father, built software to create variable-rate maps using satellite imagery.Satshot says Lanny had more than 20 years of farming experience at the time and that the idea grew from flying as a pilot over his own fields and those of neighbouring farmers in the mid-to-late 1980s. The company also links the development of the technology to difficult conditions in farming during that period. The technology has since continued under Boundri. Satshot's current website describes Satshot as a brand, service and product of Boundri Inc., and says the technology created by Lanny has continued in a new direction with Nathan Faleide. It also says Boundri will continue to run the Satshot brand, product and service "for the time being" while developing new connections and tools around mapping and imagery.The first idea was much closer to home. On Boundri's own website, Faleide says the business began with a farm-toy play rug he made for his children. He describes the family as the inspiration for Boundri and says the project grew after seeing the enjoyment his children got from the rug. DTN reported in December 2022 that Faleide had nearly 25 years of experience in precision agriculture and mapping at the time and had long wanted to do more imagery-based art. The publication reported that when he introduced an early prototype, his children began playing with their farm toys on it. A photograph of the rug was subsequently shared by a friend on Twitter, after which orders began arriving. DTN reported that about 230 orders came in while the business was still in its early stages.AgWeb also reported that the product gained attention on Twitter as the business began taking off. An autumn 2022 report from Agweek described Boundri's initial offering as generic farm-print rugs, with custom products expected to follow. The early launch eventually developed into the personalised products that now form a major part of Boundri's range. Rather than limiting the designs to generic farm scenes, the company built its products around maps and imagery connected to specific locations.Farm play rugs remain one of Boundri's main products. Its current site lists personalised farm play rugs in three sizes and also offers custom-upload rugs and other mapped products. The company says its rugs are made from polyester chenille, have hemmed edges and a no-skid polyester backing, and can be cleaned with dish soap, a rag and a hose. It also says the rugs fold for storage and are lightweight. For customers who already have their own imagery, Boundri's FAQ provides more specific instructions. It says satellite, plane or drone images can be uploaded through the company's Custom Product Builder, rather than through its main-page products. The FAQ says the files must currently be JPG or PNG and smaller than 50 MB.Boundri's product page also explains the proof process. Customers can order an item and then send a note explaining any changes they want. The company says a proof is provided before the item is printed. The business now extends beyond children's play rugs. Boundri's website lists blankets, puzzles, onesies, canvas prints and other mapped products, while its wall-map and mural work can include features such as field boundaries, attributes and other map layers. The company says these custom projects are handled on a case-by-case basis.The phrase "carpet farming" appears in both coverage of Boundri and the company's own current website. DTN used the phrase when it covered the business in 2022, while Boundri uses it on its product pages to describe the children who play with its farm rugs. Its current Custom Upload Rugs page, for example, describes the product as a gift for "little carpet farmers."The concept gives children something more specific than a generic farm-themed play surface. Boundri's products can represent actual locations, turning maps associated with farms and other meaningful places into physical objects that can be used, displayed or given as gifts. For Faleide, the business brings together two parts of his background: farming and agricultural mapping. The technology behind Satshot grew from his family's experience with agricultural imagery and mapping, while Boundri has taken that knowledge into a very different kind of product. What began with a farm-toy rug for his own children has grown into a business built around putting maps onto objects people can use and keep.
Article Summary: Nathan Faleide grew up on a farm in North Dakota and around agricultural mapping through his family's company, Satshot. The company's history dates to 1994, when Lanny Faleid built software to create variable-rate maps using satellite imagery. Today, Boundri sells mapped play rugs, blankets, wall maps and other customised products.

Article Title: ‘Time for trial and error is over’: OpenAI safety employee David Robinson quits over AI risks
Article Text:
David Robinson made the comments in an article titled "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken".

A former OpenAI safety employee has resigned from the company, warning that its rapid development of increasingly capable AI systems could raise the risk of serious failures. David Robinson said the “time for trial and error is over” and argued that AI companies need to put far greater emphasis on safety before developing more powerful systems.Robinson made the comments in an article titled "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken", published by The Atlantic on Saturday.Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and argued that safety research and expertise should play a much bigger role before more powerful AI systems are developed.Robinson spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, where he helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches. He said the company's focus on moving quickly from one AI model launch to another was making it difficult to maintain the level of caution he believed was necessary."As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed."He argued that the development of advanced AI should no longer rely on a process of repeatedly releasing systems, finding problems and fixing them afterwards.OpenAI refers to this approach as "iterative deployment", under which systems are released and their safeguards are strengthened as new problems are identified.Robinson argued that this approach is no longer sufficient as AI systems become more powerful."The time for trial and error is over," he wrote, saying advanced AI systems should have safeguards comparable to those used in high-risk fields such as nuclear power and aviation.His criticism comes amid a wider debate in the AI industry over whether companies are developing increasingly powerful systems faster than their ability to understand and control them. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have both faced scrutiny following incidents involving failed safety controls or unexpected behaviour from experimental AI systems.Robinson also warned that AI capabilities are advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment. AI alignment refers to efforts to ensure that AI systems behave in ways that are consistent with human goals and values.OpenAI defended its approach, saying it continues to put safety measures in place and can slow development when necessary."We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.
Article Summary: David Robinson said the “time for trial and error is over” and argued that AI companies need to put far greater emphasis on safety. Robinson spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, where he helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches.

Article Title: A family foundation began restoring 250 acres of overworked Ohio farmland in 1989; it is now a wildlife reserve with Walden Pond
Article Text:
The Diehl family’s 1989 project reshaped 250 acres of Ohio farmland

A man-made pond became part of the landscape

The 250-acre reserve opens its restored habitats to visitors

PC: Thoreau Wildlife Reserve

Bird nesting becomes part of the reserve’s restoration work

The reserve opened to visitors in 2020

A decades-long transformation created today’s wildlife reserve

At first glance, Thoreau Wildlife Reserve looks less like a former farm and more like a patchwork of Ohio landscapes. Meadows give way to woodland, wetlands sit alongside prairie, and older sections of forest provide another layer of habitat. Across roughly 250 acres, two miles of walking trails now lead visitors through these different settings. Yet the land did not begin this way. In 1989, the Diehl Family Foundation began a long restoration effort on farmland that had been heavily worked. More than 30 years later, the property includes a pond created by a dam, planted woodland and areas allowed to develop into more natural habitats. The reserve opened to the public in 2020.The transformation began in 1989, when the Diehl Family Foundation started a programme intended to change the character of the 250-acre property. The farmland had been heavily used, so the first stage involved preparing the soil for a different kind of landscape.According to Thoreau Wildlife Reserve, that autumn, work began on the ground itself. The following year, a dam was constructed to hold water and create what is now known as Walden Pond.A meadow was seeded, prairie was established and the first trees for a pine plantation went into the soil.The changes were not completed in a single planting season. The project continued for years as the landowners, family members, local workers and volunteers carried out further work across the property.Walden Pond is one of the clearest examples of how the reserve's present landscape was deliberately created. The water body was formed after the dam was built as part of the early restoration work. Around it, the character of the property gradually became more varied. Wetlands, prairie, hardwood woodland and areas of old growth forest now occupy parts of the reserve. Rather than replacing the farmland with one uniform type of planting, the long-running project resulted in several distinct habitats across the site.The changes also created space for a range of plants and wildlife. The reserve sits among a landscape still dominated in part by farmland, making the restored property a contrasting area of habitat.Visitors can now explore the reserve on four nature trails covering about two miles. The routes pass through meadows, woodlands, wetlands and old growth forest, giving the property several different settings within the same 250-acre site. The reserve has also been used for educational purposes. Students and faculty from Defiance College have carried out ecology studies on the property over the years, adding an academic use to the land alongside its role as a wildlife habitat.Signs placed along the trails also feature thoughts associated with H.D. Thoreau, whose ideas and writing inspired the name of the reserve.The restoration effort has extended beyond trees and vegetation. Thoreau Wildlife Reserve works with the Audubon Sanctuary Program to encourage several bird species to nest on the property, including bluebirds, wood ducks and mallard ducks.The different habitats provide a mixture of conditions across the reserve. Wet areas, woodland and open spaces each form part of the wider landscape, while the continued management of the property is intended to support wildlife living and nesting there.Although the land had been undergoing changes for decades, public access came much later. In 2020, after years of preparation, Thoreau Wildlife Reserve opened its trails to visitors. The stated purpose was to make the property available for education, recreation and appreciation of the natural environment while maintaining its role as a refuge for plants and wildlife. Opening the land also marked a new stage in a project that had begun with soil preparation and planting more than 30 years earlier.Today, access remains fairly controlled. The reserve is open from dawn until dusk, with parking available but limited. Visitors are required to remain on the designated trails, and only walking is permitted within the preserve. Dogs can be brought in, but they must remain on a lead.Visitors are asked to follow leave-no-trace principles and respect the site's natural resources. The restrictions are part of how the reserve manages public access while keeping the restored habitats intact. The property is located at 10485 Haller Road and covers approximately 250 acres. What began in 1989 as an effort to change the condition and use of heavily worked farmland has since developed into a mixture of planted and naturally developing habitats, centred partly around the man-made Walden Pond.The landscape is therefore the product of a long process rather than a single restoration project. Fields were prepared, water was held behind a new dam, trees and prairie were planted, and subsequent decades of work gradually changed the character of the property. By the time the public arrived in 2020, the site had become a wildlife reserve with trails running through several distinct ecosystems.
Article Summary: Thoreau Wildlife Reserve opened to the public in 2020 after a decades-long restoration effort. The property includes a pond created by a dam, planted woodland and areas allowed to develop into more natural habitats. Meadows give way to woodland, wetlands sit alongside prairie and older sections of forest provide another layer of habitat.

Article Title: Launched in 2020, Minecraft's Uncensored Library held around 300 books; RSF continues adding censored journalism
Article Text:
Image: Minecraft

What the Uncensored Library is and why Reporters Without Borders built it in Minecraft

Image: Minecraft

Why a video game? How Minecraft stays reachable when other platforms are blocked

How to visit the Uncensored Library, from the Minecraft server to the downloadable map

Around 300 books, twelve wings and a statue of a clenched hand holding a pen

Image: Minecraft

How the countries and articles were picked, from the Press Freedom Index to journalists' own submissions

New rooms for Brazil, Belarus, Eritrea and Iran, how the library keeps growing

What happens to a news story after authorities block or censor it? It can find another home inside a video game. In 2020, Reporters Without Borders (RSF), working with Minecraft design collective BlockWorks, launched the Uncensored Library, a vast digital archive built inside Minecraft. The project turns censored journalism into in-game books, allowing players to read reporting that may be restricted in the countries where it was originally published. The library has continued to grow. In its 2026 update, RSF added a new United States room and expanded sections dedicated to Egypt, Belarus, Russia and Iran, bringing journalism from 10 countries into the collection.Minecraft calls the Uncensored Library a grand digital library meant to combat censorship. Created by the organisation Reporters Without Borders and the Minecraft design collective BlockWorks, it was first introduced in 2020. Its purpose was to give silenced authors a platform in their own respective countries, among those that seek to censor their citizens or prevent them from accessing certain information. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library guide, written by Erika Boardman and published in 2022, adds that the library gives access to journal articles that were deemed forbidden, and that Reporters Without Borders strives to fight global censorship.The platform itself matters. As per Minecraft, social media and other platforms tend to be either blocked or controlled in the countries concerned, while Minecraft often remains accessible. That gave Reporters Without Borders a way to circumvent the censorship and make information accessible. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library calls Minecraft a popular open-world game and describes its use as a unique way to reach the younger population, while providing access to information that was condemned and hidden from the public. The finished project is a blocky book bastion, a playful phrase for a serious aim.Minecraft's article says the library is accessed through a Minecraft server, and that it can also be downloaded locally from the website. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library guide confirms that the website explains how to access the library in Minecraft. Yet, it comes with a limitation, the library is available to Windows and Mac users, but console players are out of luck, as the guide apologises to them. Anyone planning a visit should therefore read the website's instructions before setting up.According to Minecraft, the library holds around 300 books distributed between twelve wings, most of them represented by a country where information may be limited. Visitors can wander through and read banned articles presented as Minecraft books. The screenshots published in Minecraft's article offer glimpses of the setting that include a statue outside the library depicting a clenched hand with a pen, an exterior park, a book being read inside, and an Arabian floor design within the building. The imagery in the game world gives a real sense of scale, from the statue to the park.Minecraft explains that the countries in the library were selected with the help of Google Analytics, by looking at countries with an active Minecraft community as well as the Press Freedom Index published by Reporters Without Borders. Once a list had been drawn up, journalists from each of those countries then provided their articles, which were transformed into Minecraft books. The University of North Carolina at Charlotte's library says the books come from countries ranked poorly on a freedom index and include work by journalists who fought to uncover and share the truth and paid an unfortunate price for doing so. Minecraft also describes the collection as carefully curated.The Uncensored Library is regularly expanded by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), making it a collection that continues to evolve rather than a fixed archive. In its March 2026 update, RSF said the library had added a new room dedicated to the United States, while also expanding the Egypt, Belarus, Russia and Iran sections. The Belarus room received six new articles, the Russia section gained more than 20 articles from exiled media outlets, and the Egypt and Iran rooms also received new material. RSF said the library then featured journalism from Egypt, Belarus, Brazil, Eritrea, Iran, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam and the United States.The project also goes beyond Minecraft's usual role as a space for building and creativity. RSF created the virtual library as a way for journalists to make censored articles accessible, using a platform that is freely available in many countries where independent news websites may be blocked. The articles appear as books inside Minecraft and are available in English as well as the authors' native languages. Since its opening in 2020, RSF said the library had been visited more than one million times, and its books had been read 10 million times.
Article Summary: The Uncensored Library was created by Reporters Without Borders and the Minecraft design collective BlockWorks. The project turns censored journalism into in-game books, allowing players to read reporting that may be restricted in the countries where it was originally published. In its 2026 update, RSF added a new United States room and expanded sections dedicated to Egypt, Belarus, Russia and Iran.

Article Title: In 1996, Indiana turned foundry waste sand into a 275-metre highway embankment; Purdue later found the material worked successfully as full-scale road fill
Article Text:
Representative image of foundry waste sand being used as fill material to build a highway embankment. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

From foundry floors to a road embankment

What happened when the waste was put to work?

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think using foundry sand as a road-building material is a sustainable practice? Yes No 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

In 1996, Indiana embarked on an innovative project to evaluate foundry sand for use in highway construction. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

Testing whether waste could become a resource

In 1996, an unusual road-building experiment in Indiana gave an industrial waste product a second life. Instead of landfilling used foundry sand, the Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT) and Purdue University used it to build part of a highway embankment near Butler. The project covered a 275-metre section of the Country Road 37 highway project and was designed to test whether waste sand from a metal foundry could perform as a structural fill material.According to Purdue e-Pubs , the experiment was more than a laboratory test. Engineers constructed the embankment at full scale and compared the foundry-sand section with sections made using conventional clay borrow and natural sand. The researchers monitored how the materials behaved during and after construction, examining settlement, strength, water movement and other engineering characteristics.Foundry sand is reused in metal casting to make moulds and cores. However, once it is no longer useful in metal casting, large amounts of foundry sand may be treated as waste. The material used in the Indiana case study was supplied by Auburn Foundry Inc. in Auburn, Indiana. Instead of disposing of it, the material's engineering properties were investigated.According to Transportation Research Record , the 1996 demonstration used waste foundry sand from a ferrous foundry and included both WFS and control sections that were instrumented to monitor their geotechnical and environmental performance.The researchers found that the foundry sand had strength and deformation characteristics comparable to natural sand, supporting its use as structural fill. The demonstration was carried out on a full-scale section of highway embankment about 275 metres long, with engineers first constructing a test pad to determine how the material should be compacted and to assess its behaviour during construction.The scientists monitored movements within the embankment and changes in the material beneath it. Their observations involved both vertical and lateral deformations, pore water pressure, and penetration resistance. This provided a way of comparing the foundry sand layer with the other two layers of clay and natural sand. These findings were positive from a geotechnical point of view. The foundry sand displayed low internal deformations and high penetration resistance; its overall behaviour was similar to that of natural sand. It was concluded that, from the geotechnical point of view, foundry sand could be successfully used as an embankment material in highway construction projects.However, there were certain limitations to this approach. For one, the compaction of the foundry sand resulted in its low hydraulic conductivity compared to that of the natural sand, which means it could not be assumed to be a freely draining material. There was also a difficulty associated with the construction process due to the presence of foreign materials in the waste sand. Hence, foundry sand cannot be considered an appropriate substitute for all types of road building materials.Environmental performance was yet another critical factor in the demonstration process. The testing included laboratory and field tests such as bioassays and analysis of metals and other elements, as the groundwater levels were monitored within the embankment area. The results showed that there was migration of some ions from the foundry sand, although concentrations were below the relevant regulatory thresholds. The researchers thus determined that no adverse environmental effects arose from using the material.This was another practical example of why the material deserved further study. Therefore, recycling the material would lessen the need for disposal and provide construction material. Research by the Recycled Materials Resource Center estimated that the Indiana project saved about $145,000 in material costs. The Indiana test did not imply that all foundry waste could be used on roads. Different foundries produce sands with different properties, so testing and quality control are still necessary. The case showed that an industrial waste material could be processed, tested and used in a real highway project to evaluate its performance. From this perspective, the 1996 embankment construction represented a step from laboratory testing to practical application.
Article Summary: In 1996, Indiana embarked on an innovative project to evaluate foundry sand for use in highway construction. The project covered a 275-metre section of the Country Road 37 highway project. Engineers constructed the embankment at full scale and compared the foundry-sand section with sections made using conventional clay borrow and natural sand.

Article Title: In 1916, the US began releasing Asian lady beetles to control aphids and scale insects; decades later Harmonia axyridis became invasive and was linked to declines of native ladybirds
Article Text:
lady beetle

An import meant to help farmers

The first wild populations

Asian lady beetles

A familiar beetle with many faces

When helpful became harmful

A difficult species to control

A nuisance in homes too

Lessons from a century-old decision

The multicoloured Asian lady beetle was introduced to the United States with a clear purpose. Starting as early as 1916, agricultural officials released the insect, scientifically known as Harmonia axyridis, in an effort to control aphids, scale insects and other crop pests without relying as heavily on chemical insecticides. It was an appealing form of biological control, but the story took an unexpected turn. After the species established wild populations in the late 1980s, it spread rapidly across the country and beyond, becoming one of the world’s most successful invasive insects. According to reports by the USDA Agricultural Research Service, it can outcompete native ladybirds and is now regarded as an invasive species in many regions.The multicoloured Asian lady beetle is native to Asia, where it feeds on aphids and other soft-bodied arthropods. Those feeding habits made it attractive to US agricultural researchers looking for natural ways to control pests in orchards, forests, gardens and field crops. Aphids can damage plants by extracting sap, while scale insects can weaken trees and shrubs, so a predator that consumed large numbers of these pests appeared to be a useful ally.Federal, state and private entomologists released Harmonia axyridis at several locations over the years. The beetles were meant to reduce pest populations and, in turn, lower the need for insecticides. In some settings, that promise was fulfilled, especially in pecan orchards and on ornamental plants, where the beetles helped control aphids.At the time, biological control was widely viewed as a practical alternative to chemical pest management. Introducing predators can offer benefits when the predator remains focused on its target prey and fits into the new ecosystem without causing disruption. The challenge is that ecosystems are complex, and an insect that is helpful in one place can behave very differently after crossing continents.Although releases began as early as 1916, the first established US populations of multicoloured Asian lady beetles were not documented until 1988. They were found in Louisiana near the busy port of New Orleans, far from many of the locations where planned releases had occurred. That gap raised a key question: did the species establish because of intentional releases, accidental introductions through trade, or both?USDA researchers note that accidental entries likely occurred through imported nursery stock at ports in Delaware and South Carolina. This makes it difficult to trace the exact origin of the invasion. What is clear is that once Harmonia axyridis gained a foothold, it spread rapidly through North America and later across other continents.The beetle’s success was helped by its adaptability. It can survive in orchards, forests, row crops, gardens and urban areas, feeding on a broad range of prey. It also reproduces quickly, with development from egg to adult taking roughly 15 to 25 days depending on temperature and food availability. These traits gave it a major advantage in new habitats, as per the reports.The Asian lady beetle can be difficult to identify because its appearance varies greatly. Its wing covers may range from black to mustard yellow or red, and the number of spots can vary from none to many. In the United States, a common form is mustard to red with 16 or more black spots, but the diversity in colour and markings means it is not always easy to distinguish from native species at a glance.Like other ladybirds, it goes through four distinct life stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult. Females begin laying eggs on host plants in early spring, and the larvae immediately begin hunting aphids and other soft-bodied prey after hatching. Both adults and larvae are active predators, meaning the species can have a strong effect on insect populations wherever it becomes abundant.That feeding efficiency is exactly what made the beetle valuable to agriculture. However, a voracious appetite is not limited to crop pests. It can also put pressure on native ladybirds that depend on the same food sources, turning an agricultural helper into a conservation concern.The USDA describes the Asian lady beetle as a mixed blessing. It remains an effective predator of aphids and other pests, but has also become a nuisance in homes and a threat to biodiversity. In invaded countries Harmonia axyridis is considered invasive as it can outcompete other ladybug species for food and habitat.Native ladybugs might be unable to compete with a highly adaptable newcomer moving into the same ecological niche. Harmonia axyridis is larger than many native species, highly mobile and able to use a wide range of habitats. Its ability to find food across different crops and landscapes can give it an advantage when prey is scarce.The beetle also has strong defences. USDA research notes that it possesses chemical, mechanical and microbiological anti-predator traits that cause many predators to avoid it. These defences reduce the natural pressure that might otherwise limit its numbers, allowing populations to increase and spread.Scientists have studied whether predators and parasitoids could naturally slow the Asian lady beetle’s expansion. The evidence suggests that many vertebrate and invertebrate predators in invaded regions are relatively ineffective at limiting the beetle. Some birds and insects can consume it, but its defensive adaptations often make it an unappealing or difficult target.Parasitoids, organisms that develop on or inside a host and ultimately kill it, may offer some potential. USDA researchers identified certain true flies in the genus Phalacrotophora as possible natural enemies capable of overcoming some of the beetle’s defences. However, researchers stress that more work is needed to understand whether these relationships can meaningfully reduce populations at a larger scale.The case of Harmonia axyridis illustrates a common pattern in biological invasions. A species introduced without its full set of predators, parasites and ecological constraints may initially flourish. Over time, native species may adapt and new relationships may form, but that process can take years or decades and may not undo the harm already caused.For homeowners, the most visible problem often arrives in autumn. As temperatures drop, adult Asian lady beetles seek sheltered places to overwinter, including homes, sheds and other buildings. They are particularly drawn to light-coloured structures, such as white, grey and yellow houses, which can act as visual cues for the insects.The beetles do not damage structures in the way termites or carpenter ants do. They do not chew wood, bore through walls, feed on carpets, or lay eggs indoors. However, they can gather in large numbers in wall spaces and then enter living areas on warm winter or early spring days while searching for an exit.When disturbed or crushed, the insects can release a yellow, unpleasant-smelling fluid from their leg joints as a defence called reflex bleeding. The fluid can stain walls and fabrics, making the beetles unwelcome indoors despite being pest predators. USDA guidance recommends sealing cracks and crevices outside homes before autumn and using a vacuum or broom to remove beetles that get inside.The Asian lady beetle’s journey from a planned pest-control import to a widespread invasive species offers an important lesson about ecological caution. Biocontrol reduces pesticide use and protects crops, but all nonnative species come with risks that aren’t always immediately apparent. A predator may control one pest while competing with native species or creating new problems elsewhere.More than a century after the first US releases, Harmonia axyridis remains both useful and disruptive. It still has some use controlling aphids in certain agricultural settings, but the unintended consequences of its spread have come at a cost to native ladybugs and home comfort. Its history is a warning that even well-meaning attempts to help the environment have to be assessed not just on the benefits they bring in the short term, but on what they might lead to in the longer term.
Article Summary: The multicoloured Asian lady beetle is native to Asia, where it feeds on aphids and other soft-bodied arthropods. In the late 1980s, the species established wild populations in the US. It spread rapidly across the country and beyond, becoming one of the world’s most successful invasive insects. According to reports by the USDA Agricultural Research Service, it can outcompete native ladybirds.

Article Title: A 1987 Buick GNX, No. 450 of just 547 built for a single model year, sold for $200,000 with 26 miles in 2024; two years and only 4 miles later, the 30-mile car sold again for $427,000
Article Text:
Inside, the GNX remains unmistakably rooted in its era. A three-spoke leather-wrapped steering wheel sits ahead of GNX-specific Stewart-Warner instrumentation.

From $200,000 to $427,000

Built to end the Grand National era

A turbocharged V6 with serious muscle

Preserved almost exactly as delivered

Why the GNX remains collectible

Some cars age and others simply become more expensive to own. A 1987 Buick GNX with barely 30 miles on its odometer has demonstrated just how dramatically collector demand can shift, selling for $427,000 after changing hands for $200,000 only two years earlier, states an online report by Bring A Trailer. The black performance coupe, number 450 of just 547 GNXs built for the model year, has covered only four additional miles since its previous sale, adds the online report.According to September 2026 report by Bring A Trailer, the GNX previously sold on Bring a Trailer in July 2024 with 26 miles on the odometer. It has since been acquired by the dealer now offering the car in Texas, with the mileage increasing to just 30 miles. The latest transaction more than doubled the car's previous sale price, highlighting the premium attached to exceptionally preserved examples of one of the most sought-after American performance cars of the 1980s.The car comes with manufacturer literature, memorabilia, copies of its original window sticker, a clean Carfax report and a clean California title, adds the report.The Grand National Experimental, or GNX, was developed as a final celebration of Buick's Grand National production run.Buick partnered with McLaren Performance Technologies and ASC to turn the already formidable Grand National into a limited-production performance model. Only 547 examples were produced, all in black, making the cars instantly recognizable. The GNX added a collection of visual and mechanical upgrades, including composite wheel-arch flares, heat-extracting fender vents, GNX badging, sport mirrors, dual exhaust outlets and a distinctive three-piece rear spoiler, reads the online report. The car also rides on 16-inch cross-lace wheels and features a limited-slip differential, air conditioning and cruise control.If we go by the report, under the hood is a turbocharged 3.8-liter V6 modified by ASC/McLaren. The engine received a Garrett T3 turbocharger, a larger air-to-air intercooler and a lower-restriction exhaust system. Factory output was rated at 276 horsepower and 360 lb-ft of torque. Power reaches the rear wheels through a 200R4 four-speed automatic transmission fitted with an upgraded oil cooler. A GNX-branded aluminum cover distinguishes the limited-slip differential at the rear.The suspension was also reworked and the GNX retained front suspension components from the contemporary Grand National while gaining upgraded rear hardware, including a Panhard rod, torque arm and additional frame crossmember. Power-assisted front disc brakes and rear drums handle stopping duties.Inside, the GNX remains unmistakably rooted in its era. A three-spoke leather-wrapped steering wheel sits ahead of GNX-specific Stewart-Warner instrumentation. The instrument cluster includes a 160-mph speedometer, an 8,000-rpm tachometer and dedicated gauges monitoring turbo boost, oil pressure, coolant temperature and fuel level. The five-digit odometer now reads just 30 miles, making the car less a used performance machine than a remarkably preserved snapshot of Buick's brief but significant assault on the American performance-car market.The GNX arrived at the end of an era when turbocharged American cars were beginning to challenge expectations about what a large domestic coupe could do. Its limited production, McLaren-developed mechanical upgrades and distinctive appearance have since made it a cornerstone of 1980s performance-car collecting. For this particular example, the jump from $200,000 to $427,000 in just two years, and with only four additional miles, adds another chapter to that collector story.Image Courtesy: Bring A Trailer
Article Summary: A 1987 Buick GNX with barely 30 miles on its odometer has sold for $427,000 after changing hands for $200,000 only two years earlier. The black performance coupe, number 450 of just 547 GNXs built for the model year, has covered only four additional miles since its previous sale. The latest transaction more than doubled the car's previous sale price, highlighting the premium attached to exceptionally preserved examples of the car.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

Is Aadhaar mandatory for a digital Life Certificate



Legal validity of Jeevan Pramaan



How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: ChatGPT for Teens: 5 features parents should know about, from homework help to screen time controls
Article Text:
Study Mode: guided learning instead of instant answers

Homework reminders that nudge teens away from shortcuts

Turning tough topics into quizzes and interactive visuals

Parental controls that set structure without constant monitoring

Smarter prompts can make revision genuinely more productive

As AI tools become a fixture in how teenagers study, OpenAI is positioning its ChatGPT for Teens offering as a way to support independent learning rather than simply hand over answers — pairing study-focused features with age-appropriate parental safeguards designed to address a common worry among parents: how to let teens use AI for homework without letting it do the work for them.At the center of ChatGPT for Teens is Study Mode, which turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. Rather than jumping straight to a final answer, it breaks concepts down step by step, offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.Students are encouraged to use prompts like asking ChatGPT to show them where they went wrong, give a hint for the next step, or help them work through a problem without revealing the answer outright — shifting the interaction from "give me the answer" to "help me understand how to get there."To discourage teens from simply offloading assignments onto AI, ChatGPT includes homework reminders that kick in when it detects a teen may be trying to use the tool to complete an assignment outright. Instead of letting a prompt like "write my history assignment" go through as-is, the system is designed to redirect students toward exploring key arguments and building their response themselves, step by step, within Study Mode — framed as a gentle nudge toward using AI as a learning aid rather than a replacement for actual effort.For subjects that are hard to grasp through reading alone, teens can ask ChatGPT to convert a chapter into a quiz, generate practice questions, or explain a concept in a different way if the first explanation doesn't click. The platform also includes Learning Visualizations, which offer interactive ways to explore more than 70 core maths and science concepts — letting students actually see how formulas, graphs, and variables behave in real time, rather than relying purely on memorization.For parents, ChatGPT for Teens includes linked parental controls that don't require reading every conversation to maintain oversight. Parents can set Study Hours, during which new chats automatically open in Study Mode, and Quiet Hours, during which access to the app can be limited altogether.Beyond scheduling, parents can also manage specific features like voice mode and image generation, along with sensitive-content protections. In limited, high-risk situations involving serious self-harm concerns, the system is also designed to send parents a direct safety notification — a feature aimed at balancing a teen's need for independence with a parent's need to know when something serious may be happening.Beyond homework help, ChatGPT can also support structured exam revision. Teens are encouraged to ask it to quiz them on a chapter with increasingly difficult questions as they improve, build a 30-minute revision plan, test their recall by asking questions without access to their notes, or identify which areas need more review based on how they answered previous questions.Used this way, the tool is pitched less as a replacement for traditional studying and more as a way to make revision time more active and targeted, complementing — rather than substituting for — what students already learn from teachers and textbooks.
Article Summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens lets teens use AI to help them learn. Study Mode turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. It offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.

Article Title: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third happened this year when he looked closely at...
Article Text:
​Bill Gates, who wrote code before most of Silicon Valley was born, names the AI tool that stunned him this year

Bill Gates says coding is where AI's progress surprised him most

Gates expects AI to reshape software engineering jobs first

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third came this year when he looked closely at Anthropic's AI coding tool, Claude Code. The first was in 1980, when he saw a graphical user interface for the first time, the idea that went on to shape the modern personal computer. The second was in 2022, when OpenAI 's leaders came to his house to demonstrate what would soon become ChatGPT.Claude Code hit differently because of what it does. Gates wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people, and he calls it the subject he knows best. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said in a recent interview.Gates's reaction carries weight because of where he started. He began programming as a teenager in Seattle, and in 1975 he co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen on the back of software they wrote themselves. For most of his life, writing good code was the skill that set him apart.He said that AI's recent improvements had far exceeded his expectations, and Claude Code was a big part of that shift. It was also one of the reasons he chose to speak out now.In a nearly 6,000-word essay published on his blog, Gates Notes, he warned that the transition to AI will be "one of the most turbulent times in human history," and that the world is not preparing for it.Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. Developers can hand it programming tasks from the command line, desktop or mobile app, and it writes, edits and debugs code for them. Anthropic showcased it at its Code with Claude developer event in May.Gates has been tracking AI's impact on programmers for a while. Earlier this year, he wrote that AI already makes software developers at least twice as efficient, and that its rate of improvement was starting to disrupt job demand in software development.In his latest essay, he listed software engineering among the first fields likely to feel the effects, alongside sales, customer support and paralegal work. He did offer one caveat. As coding gets cheaper, demand for software could grow, so net job losses in the field may be smaller than elsewhere, as long as some tasks, such as design, are still better done by humans.Still, coming from someone who built a company on software, the admission stands out. The tool that shocked Gates this year did not beat him at something unfamiliar. It beat him at the thing he knows best.
Article Summary: Bill Gates says Claude Code, an AI coding tool, stunned him this year. He wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said.

Article Title: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed
Article Text:
OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed

Alleged sharing of information with AI safety group

The connection to the Hugging Face breach

Part of a bigger reckoning inside OpenAI

A moment of mounting pressure on AI safety practices

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has terminated three researchers from its safety team after an internal investigation concluded that they violated company policies governing access to and handling of sensitive information, according to a company statement and a Wall Street Journal report. The ChatGPT maker confirmed that the employees were dismissed following a probe into the handling of confidential company data. "We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," an OpenAI spokesperson said. "Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work."According to a Wall Street Journal report, the three researchers are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, all of whom worked on safety and alignment-related efforts at the company.The report said the researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations, including nonprofit research groups involved in evaluating advanced AI systems.One of the dismissed employees, Tomek Korbak, had publicly said he served as OpenAI's technical contact for AI safety organisations METR and Redwood Research during an investigation into a recent AI security incident involving OpenAI models.The other two researchers, Wang and Balesni, worked on AI alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems behave in accordance with human intentions and safety objectives. Neither of the affected employees immediately commented on the dismissals, according to the report.The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment, including an incident in which one of its models hacked AI platform Hugging Face. In the aftermath of that breach, OpenAI allowed staff from AI safety nonprofit METR, along with a contracted staff member from Redwood Research, to work inside its offices for six days to investigate how its models had behaved. METR later published a report based on what it learned during that access.Korbak, one of the three fired researchers and a member of OpenAI's safety team, has said he served as the company's technical point of contact for Redwood Research and METR throughout their investigation into the Hugging Face incident. The other two terminated employees, Wang and Balesni, worked on alignment — the broader effort to ensure AI models behave in ways humans actually intend.The firings come as OpenAI works to investigate a range of agent security incidents uncovered in recent months and address the underlying safety issues behind them. Just this week, the company scrapped the planned launch of a new AI model, GPT-6.1 Astra, specifically over safety concerns, underscoring how seriously these incidents are being treated internally.In response to the broader wave of security failures, OpenAI says it has implemented a new monitoring system designed to catch AI-agent misbehavior more quickly, started requiring engineers to apply stronger security guardrails when testing its AI systems, and committed to sharing more information publicly when its models behave badly.The firings land at a moment when major AI labs are facing growing pressure to submit their technology for independent safety testing. Just last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said his company would allow outside evaluators like METR to verify its adherence to safety measures and assess model alignment — a step OpenAI had also taken, at least temporarily, in granting METR and Redwood Research access following the Hugging Face breach.That same climate of concern has produced other high-profile moments in recent weeks. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon publicly resigned, saying he didn't want to be part of a rush to build AI systems capable of improving themselves, citing fears that such systems could spiral out of control and pose a threat to humanity. Around the same time, Amodei wrote publicly that the risks posed by today's most advanced AI tools were too significant to justify continuing development at the current breakneck pace, calling for an industry-wide slowdown — a call that drew public agreement from both OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
Article Summary: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed. The researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations. The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment.

Article Title: Google ex-CEO Eric Schmidt: Best programmers don't write code anymore, they...
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt's idea of a top programmer goes to bed at 7 PM

The best programmers won't be replaced by AI—they'll become even more valuable

Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run—and go to bed. It's a shift that Schmidt believes signals something much larger than a change in workflow—it's the beginning of AI reshaping how entire industries operate.Schmidt described a programmer at one of his startups who does exactly this. Every evening at 7 PM, he defines what he wants the AI to build, writes a test function to judge the output, and lets the system loose. Then he has dinner with his wife and goes to sleep. The AI churns through the night, finishing around 4 AM. By breakfast, the work is done. "This stuff would've taken me six months and 10 programmers at Google," Schmidt said. "This poor guy's sleeping."The natural assumption is that AI will make programmers obsolete. Schmidt thinks the opposite is true—at least for the elite ones. Top-tier engineers were always disproportionately valuable, worth roughly 10 times more than those just below them. That gap, he argued, is about to widen.The grunt work is disappearing, but the ability to orchestrate AI systems at scale—grasping parallelisation, defining the right constraints, judging when the output is good enough—is becoming the entire job.The real skill now isn't writing code, Schmidt suggested. It's framing the problem correctly and knowing what "good" looks like. "If you can define the evaluation function and you can let it run, and if you have enough hardware, you're inventing worlds," he said. AI systems at leading research labs are already handling a significant and growing share of programming work, making the engineers who direct them more critical, not less.Yet the bigger story, Schmidt argued, isn't about programmers at all. AI's largest economic payoff will come from automating the dull, expensive plumbing of corporate operations—billing, accounting, inventory management, delivery logistics—processes that silently drain billions from company budgets every year. "If anything, it's under-hyped because you are fundamentally automating businesses," he said at Harvard's John F. Kennedy Jr. Forum.He predicted artificial general intelligence could arrive as early as 2029, powered by recursive self-improvement—AI systems that learn and plan on their own, without waiting for human instruction. Schmidt also pointed to medicine, climate solutions, and engineering as fields where AI-driven automation could unlock breakthroughs that remain largely untapped today.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run and go to bed. Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business operations.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what

Yann LeCun criticises AI safety warnings

Yann LeCun, widely known as the “godfather of AI”, does not believe artificial intelligence (AI) will wipe out humanity. Instead, LeCun says recent incidents in which AI agents hacked company networks and other systems were caused by poor human oversight and badly designed security systems. Speaking about the risks linked to AI agents, Yann LeCun said told Fortune: “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” adding that the systems were supposed to operate inside secure sandboxes. “They were supposed to be in sandboxes, but the sandboxes were leaky and horribly designed,” he said.Yann LeCun, who shared the 2018 Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning, said he has “zero concerns” about recent rogue AI incidents and is not worried “at all” about AI destroying humanity.He said incidents such as an OpenAI agent autonomously hacking Hugging Face could have been prevented through better system design and oversight. LeCun also argued that some AI labs do not have a strong enough understanding of cybersecurity. He said the risks from AI agents should be addressed through better safeguards rather than broad claims about AI becoming an existential threat.During the interaction, Yann LeCun has also criticised the growing focus on AI safety, particularly ideas linked to the effective altruism movement.He called the movement “super toxic” and a “complete disaster.”He also criticised warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Amodei, LeCun said, is “honest”, but he accused him of supporting policies that could benefit large AI companies by making it harder for smaller competitors and open-source developers to compete.“Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ‘saying, ‘AI can kill us all’ is incredibly destructive for everybody, including for the public who’s scared shitless,” LeCun said. He called such messaging “the worst marketing campaign you can possibly imagine.”
